text:
Rajesh Kumar: Hey team — running a ramp load test and starting around ~5k RPS we get a flood of 429s from /v1/completions. Clients retry immediately and we end up with duplicate completions and what looks like double billing for some customers. Any quick troubleshooting pointers?

Maya Chen: Oof. Can you paste one or two raw request/response pairs (headers + body) and the SDK version the client is using? Also did you see a Retry-After header in the 429?

Rajesh Kumar: Pasting a sanitized example below. SDK is our official JS SDK v1.4.2. We saw Retry-After sometimes but not always.
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"say hi","max_tokens":50}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:03:21 GMT
X-Request-Id: req_01F...
Retry-After: 3
Content-Type: application/json

{"error": {"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"request rate exceeded","retry_after":3}}
```

Devon Patel: Quick notes from SDK side: default JS SDK v1.4.2 retry defaults are: max_retries=4, backoff_base=0.5s, backoff_multiplier=2.0, jitter=full, and we respect Retry-After headers when present. But crucially the SDK does NOT inject an Idempotency-Key by default for completion endpoints — we left that opt-in because many completions are non-idempotent (streaming/stateful).

Devon Patel: If users are doing synchronous completions (non-stream) you can make retries safer by adding an `Idempotency-Key` header/client param. Server will dedupe identical keys for a short TTL and return the original response when the key is seen again. Example (JS):
```js
client.completions.create({
  model: 'redwood-large',
  prompt: 'say hi',
  max_tokens: 50,
  headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'user-order-1234' }
})
```

Devon Patel: For streaming: idempotency is harder. We recommend a client-side dedupe (track request signature + timestamp) or encode enough state in the idempotency key and store on your side.

Samir Li: From infra — when quota is exhausted we use a leaky-bucket algorithm per API key with a burst allowance. If burst > burst_capacity you'll see 429s without Retry-After (we send Retry-After only when we have a deterministic time to serve). Clients must back off with jitter. If this customer is frequently hitting sustained bursts, we can increase their burst window temporarily.

Maya Chen: Rajesh — can you share which endpoints (batch completions vs streaming vs chat) and whether the duplicate output equals duplicate invoice lines? If billing double-counting is suspected, include invoice ids.

Rajesh Kumar: It's chat-like completions over websocket and some REST calls. The duplicated items in billing appear as multiple usage lines with same timestamps. Not 100% sure yet if it's retries or the test itself was firing duplicates.

Devon Patel: A couple of pragmatic suggestions: 1) Respect server Retry-After when present. 2) Use exponential backoff with full jitter when Retry-After absent. 3) Add an Idempotency-Key on any request that creates billable objects. 4) Limit client-side retry attempts for non-idempotent endpoints (default to 0-1 retries).

Devon Patel: Example backoff pseudocode we recommend in SDK docs:
```
base = 0.5s
for attempt in 1..max_retries:
  wait = random_uniform(0, base * 2^(attempt-1))  # full jitter
  sleep(wait)
  call()
```
Maya Chen: Repro steps we used to see the issue:
- Run k6 with 200 concurrent VUs hitting /v1/chat/completions over 60s ramp.
- Some tests used clients that retried immediately on 429 with no idempotency key.
- Observe 429 spikes, then the same request id appears multiple times in request logs.

Rajesh Kumar: Logs snippet from our gateway (sanitized):
```
[14:03:21] req=req_01F... api_key=acct_789 status=429 route=/v1/completions client_id=svc-loadtest
[14:03:22] req=req_01F... api_key=acct_789 status=200 route=/v1/completions client_id=svc-loadtest
```
This looks like client retried and later got a 200 for the same logical operation.

Samir Li: That lines up: server will sometimes accept a later retry when capacity free — which results in duplicate processing if the original attempt had side effects (e.g., billing record created before the 429 was returned). Server-side we try to make create operations idempotent when an Idempotency-Key is provided, but without it the app must handle dedupe.

Maya Chen: Action items:
- Rajesh: collect a small set of request ids + invoice ids and attach to the ticket.
- Samir: can you check acct_789 quota history and temporary burst config?
- Devon: add a short snippet and note to SDK docs about idempotency for completions + recommended retry settings.

deploy-bot: Created support ticket INC-4521 for acct_789 (severity: high).

Devon Patel: We should probably tighten SDK defaults for next patch: lower default retries for chat/streaming to 1 and add an opt-in idempotency helper util that can generate keys and attach them automatically to sync completions. Will file a PR.

Samir Li: I checked quota history — acct_789 exceeded sustained QPS thresholds during the load window and consumed burst credits. I can raise their burst allowance for 24h while they finish testing. Doing now (applied temporary policy + note in INC-4521).

Rajesh Kumar: Thanks all — I'll attach the request ids to the ticket and rerun with idempotency keys turned on for sync calls and backoff changes on clients. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Marking for follow-up docs; Devon please ping when PR is up. (reacted with :eyes:)
